Let
\[
u=x^2,\qquad v=y^3.
\]
Since \(dx\) over both signs of \(x\) gives \(u^{-1/2}du\), and
\[
dy=\frac13 |v|^{-2/3}dv,
\]
we get
\[
I_n=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-nw^2}H(w)\,dw,
\]
where
\[
H(w)=\frac13\int_0^\infty u^{-1/2}|u-w|^{-2/3}
e^{-|u-w|^{2/3}}\,du.
\]

As \(w\to0^\pm\), scaling \(u=|w|s\) gives
\[
H(w)=D_\pm |w|^{-1/6}+\frac12\Gamma\!\left(-\frac14\right)+o(1).
\]
The one-sided leading constants are
\[
D_-=\frac13B\!\left(\frac12,\frac16\right),
\]
and
\[
D_+=\frac13\left[
B\!\left(\frac12,\frac13\right)+B\!\left(\frac13,\frac16\right)
\right].
\]
Using the beta-gamma identities,
\[
D_++D_-=
\frac{(3+\sqrt3)\Gamma(1/6)\Gamma(1/3)}{6\sqrt\pi}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac12\Gamma\!\left(\frac5{12}\right)(D_++D_-)=C_0,
\]
so the given subtraction removes exactly the cusp leading term.

The remaining constant term contributes
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-nw^2}\left(\frac12\Gamma\!\left(-\frac14\right)\right)\,dw
=
\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2}\Gamma\!\left(-\frac14\right)n^{-1/2}.
\]
Since \(\Gamma(3/4)=(-1/4)\Gamma(-1/4)\), this equals
\[
-2\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma\!\left(\frac34\right)n^{-1/2}.
\]

Hence
\[
\boxed{-2\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma\!\left(\frac34\right)}.
\]
